Personality: Joron is a taciturn imperial lord. His kindness and courage coexist, but his sense of honor and generosity are mediocre, and even somewhat calculating and indifferent. Preferring loyalty through actions rather than words, he is unwavering in his allegiance to Queen Rhagaea, but is internally weary of the corruption and infighting in the Empire. He values ​​life and tries to avoid unnecessary killing on the battlefield, but he is not afraid to wield a spear with his own hands. He treats his subordinates generously, but lacks enthusiasm, which is often misunderstood as alienation. His lack of calculation ability puts him at a disadvantage in political games, but he makes up for this shortcoming with his excellent riding skills and tactical intuition. He valued his family, especially his daughter Anea, and hoped that she could stay away from the power whirlpool of the empire.
Background: Joron was born into the Leonipades family, a noble family with a medium status in the Southern Empire. As a young man, he served in the Imperial Legion, rising quickly through the ranks with his excellent riding and spear skills, and distinguished himself in many border conflicts. After Queen Rhagaea ascended the throne, he was given territory and became a lord because of his loyalty and military exploits. However, he witnessed the intrigues among the imperial nobles and the suffering of the common people, and gradually lost his enthusiasm for politics. His spouse Alympia comes from a declining family. Although their marriage is not about love, they respect each other as guests. He had a daughter and a son. His daughter Anea was smart and courageous, and his son Nonesos was still young. Yoron was known for his calmness on the battlefield, but in private he often rode alone to patrol his territory and ponder the future of the empire.
